title: Ingress surge tiling allocation sheet — regional AZ buffer proforma
content:
Purpose:
Quick working sheet to translate observed Q2 microburst shapes into a region-by-region GPU tiling + AZ buffer proforma. Lightweight, calc-first, intended to produce a recommended tile size and safety buffer per AZ for routing and prewarm logic.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Measured 95th pct microburst for text-generation (1250-token median requests) across last 30 days shows 18% of 1h windows contain a 3–15min spike that is ~3.2x baseline in tokens/sec in NA-west region.
- Proposed mitigation = AZ-level GPU tiling + 15% per-AZ safety stock + cross-AZ overflow routing.
- Target: keep P95 tail latency under 600ms for request sizes <=1k tokens at target util <=72% across production pools.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU varies by model class and quantization profile. Use the following conservative estimates for planning:
  - llama-70b-q4: 28k tokens/sec/GPU (serving config: kv-cache active, batching disabled for tail)
  - opt-6.7b-fp16: 95k tokens/sec/GPU
  - redwood-mix-30b-int8: 40k tokens/sec/GPU
- Baseline routed mix (hosted-api): 48% small completions (<128 tokens), 40% standard (~512 tokens), 12% long (>1024 tokens).
- Cache/prefix savings: average 12% token reduction in steady-state; during new-spike cold-prefix we assume 0% savings.
- We budget for 15% traffic growth over 30 days (for surge runway comparisons).

Region / AZ snapshot (sourced from metrics pipeline, 2026-07-01 .. 2026-07-09):
Columns: Region | AZs | Primary GPU families | Allocated nodes | GPUs total | Measured baseline tokens/sec (median) | 95th microburst multiplier
NA-west | 3 AZs | H100-80GB, H200 | 180 nodes | 360 GPUs | 1,200,000 tps | 3.2
NA-east | 3 AZs | H100-80GB | 120 nodes | 240 GPUs | 800,000 tps | 2.6
EU-west | 3 AZs | H200, A100-mix | 110 nodes | 220 GPUs | 650,000 tps | 2.9
APAC-sg | 2 AZs | A100, T4-ev | 50 nodes | 100 GPUs | 220,000 tps | 3.8

Interpretation and quick math (conservative):
- Convert GPU counts to effective tokens/sec capacity using model mix weighted average. Example NA-west: assume mix leads to weighted eff = 32k tps/GPU -> cap = 360 * 32k = 11.52M tps. Provisioned baseline usage = 1.2M tps -> measured utilization = 10.4% (we're compute-rich today; but note many GPUs pinned to large-model private workloads and dedicated pools, this sheet focuses only on Hosted API pool share).
- Microburst capacity need = baseline * 95th multiplier. For NA-west: 1.2M * 3.2 = 3.84M tps. Shortfall relative to capacity = 3.84M - 11.52M = negative (i.e., capacity raw is enough). But practical constraints: shard/tiling/placement can create hot-AZ exhaustion even when global capacity looks ok.

Per-AZ tiling proposal (goal = isolate spikes to AZ and keep P95 latency < target):
- Tile size = number of GPUs per routing shard. Lower tile size -> better isolation but higher replication overhead.
- Proposed initial tile sizes: 8, 16, 32 GPUs.
- Compute per-AZ tile count = floor(AZ GPUs / tile size). Example NA-west (360 GPUs / 3 AZs = 120 GPUs/AZ):
  - tile=8 -> 15 tiles/AZ (120/8=15)
  - tile=16 -> 7 tiles/AZ (floor 7)
  - tile=32 -> 3 tiles/AZ

Safety buffer and overflow policy:
- Per-AZ safety buffer = max(15% of tile capacity, 1 tile) to cover short prewarm latency and scheduling churn.
- Cross-AZ overflow: route to sibling AZ with available tile capacity if local buffer exhausted; prefer AZ with same GPU family to preserve perf profile.
- Global fallback: route to a lower-cost quantized variant (redwood-mix-30b-int8) if sibling AZs are exhausted.

Scenario modelling (text snapshots of simple calculations):
- Scenario A (Conservative / worst microburst case): assume 3.2x spike sustained for 10min, no cache savings, 15% growth.
  - NA-west AZ baseline = 1.2M/3 AZ = 400k tps/AZ. Spike = 400k * 3.2 * 1.15 = 1.472M tps/AZ.
  - Tile capacity (tile=16, eff 32k tps/GPU): tile cap = 16 * 32k = 512k tps.
  - Required tiles to absorb spike (with 15% tile buffer): needed = ceil(1.472M / (512k * 0.85)) = ceil(1.472M / 435,200) = 4 tiles -> 4*16 = 64 GPUs -> available per AZ = 120 GPUs so OK.
- Scenario B (Optimistic / short microburst): 2.0x spike, cache 12% savings, growth 5% -> required tiles drop to 2 tiles.
- Scenario C (AZ outage simultaneous with spike): assume local AZ loses 50% of tiles -> overflow pressure to sibling AZs; need cross-AZ route capacity and prewarming latency budget (target prewarm < 18s).

Operational knobs (actions/notes):
- Prewarm policy: keep 1 tile per AZ warm for top 10% models (by traffic) + on-demand async prewarm for others. Track prewarm success rate; target success rate >= 98%.
- Autoscaler: implement fast-path for short microbursts (<5m): prefer lightweight pod-level scaling (increase concurrency/batching) over full node adds.
- Routing: update policy to prefer same-family AZ first; only route cross-family when predicted latency impact < 10% and token-cost delta acceptable.

Cost heuristics (approx):
- Cost per H100 GPU hour = $X (placeholder) -> show rough: H100 slot hourly = $4.6 (est). 1 extra tile (16 H100s) for 10min surge -> cost = 16 * 4.6 * (10/60) ~ $122.7 per surge event. Use these to justify reserved keep-warm budget.

Open questions / flags: 
- How many models must be kept cross-AZ warm vs on cold start? (data needed: model traffic share by tail contributions).
- Prewarm latency: current telemetry sometimes shows 25–40s on cold for very large models. Need infra + runtime fast-path to push this under 18s for safety stock to be effective.
- Placement constraints: some dedicated and private customers reserve whole nodes; confirm actual Hosted pool slice per AZ vs reported total GPUs above.

Immediate next steps (owner/action/ETA):
- Run a finer-grain analysis of model-level tail contributions (Samira) -> JIRA-ENGINF-2346 -> due 2026-07-26
- Prototype tile-size 16 routing simulation in staging with replayed Q2 microbursts (Alex) -> branch: infra/tile-sim-16 -> due 2026-07-30
- Add prewarm telemetry KPI to SLO dashboard and alert if cold-start > 18s for top 20 models (Ethan) -> due 2026-07-25

Quick notes to reviewers:
- This sheet is intentionally conservative and assumes low cache during surge. If you believe cache effectiveness during spikes is higher, we can tighten buffers.
- We should compare two deployment experiments: (A) smaller tiles (8) but higher warm replication vs (B) larger tiles (32) with cross-AZ overflow. Pros/cons listed inline in the staging doc linked above.

Appendix: sample tile math (copyable):
- AZ_spike_tps = (region_baseline_tps / AZ_count) * burst_multiplier * (1 + growth_pct)
- tile_capacity = tile_size * eff_tps_per_gpu * quant_adjust
- needed_tiles = ceil(AZ_spike_tps / (tile_capacity * (1 - safety_pct)))

End of sheet.

(Informal notes/bullet doodles below — ignore if using formal planning doc):
- If we pre-allocate 1 tile per AZ for top-10 models, that answers many short spikes; main cost is warm memory reservation, not GPU hours.
- Look into KV cache sticky routing to reduce cross-AZ overhead for sessions.
- Consider a transient cheap-tier fallback (quantized in same AZ) for very short blips to avoid cross-AZ egress.
